verdicts.rationale: The sole divergence hint is the shield's 250% Dendro absorption effectiveness. That is a defensive damage-absorption magnitude, not something the timeline renders: the timeline shows the shield's duration window (12s, refresh-on-recast) which is already modeled, never an absorption amount or per-element effectiveness value, so there is no rendered surface to diverge from. Per-element shield efficiency is a damage-absorption calculation excluded by the 'visualize mechanics, never calculate verdicts' constitution, and there is no wired per-element shield-efficiency primitive, so it is neither addable nor implementable. The stacked-absorption ceiling is likewise a magnitude with no rendered surface. Nothing affecting rotation reading is misrepresented.

groundedIn.claim: The shield's 250% Dendro absorption effectiveness is not modeled because there is no element-specific shield-efficiency field.
groundedIn.quote: Shield absorbs Dendro DMG with 250% effectiveness — not modeled (schema has no element-specific shield-effectiveness field).

groundedIn.claim: The 250% effectiveness is a defensive absorption magnitude, not a rotation-timing surface.
groundedIn.quote: The shield will absorb Dendro DMG with 250% effectiveness. The shield's DMG absorption will be based on Kirara's Max HP and will not exceed a certain percentage of that Max HP.

groundedIn.claim: The shield window itself (duration and refresh-on-recast) is already authored and modeled, so the rotation-relevant surface is not diverging.
groundedIn.quote: durationType 'refresh': on recast the remaining absorption stacks onto the new shield and the 12s duration resets…

verdicts.rationale: The divergence hint is C1's up-to-4 extra cardamoms, which is a scaling projectile/damage-instance count on the burst summon. The timeline renders the Cat Grass Cardamoms summon as a 12s stationary window with no tick markers and no count; the cardamom quantity (6 base, +4 at C1) is never rendered, so there is no surface to diverge from. Projectile/hit count is a damage-output detail excluded by the no-damage-numbers constitution, and there is no wired 'scaling projectile count on a summon' primitive, so it is neither addable nor implementable. The summon lifetime — the only rotation-relevant fact — is modeled correctly.

groundedIn.claim: C1's extra cardamoms are a scaling count on the summon's projectile count, not modeled on the burst summon.
groundedIn.quote: C1 adds up to 4 extra cardamoms (1 per 8000 Max HP) — a scaling buff on the summon's projectile count, not a damage scaling on existing hits. Flagged on the C1 constellation entry; not modeled on the burst summon.

groundedIn.claim: The rendered surface is the summon lifetime, not the cardamom count or per-cardamom behavior.
groundedIn.quote: Schema's stationary `summons[]` represents the lifetime; per-cardamom contact-trigger semantics aren't modeled.
